feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=2x-{y}^{3},\,y(0.5)=1
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step and Newton's method to approximate $y(1).$ Round your answer to two decimal places.

$y(1)≈$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=1,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=1-0.5=0.5.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((2x-{y}^{3})+(2{x}_{\text{new}}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}))\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.5x-0.25{y}^{3}+0.5{x}_{\text{new}}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.5x-0.25{y}^{3}+0.5{x}_{\text{new}}-0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{3},\end{aligned}
$$

and moving all terms to the left-hand side gives the equation

$$
0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}+{y}_{\text{new}}+0.25{y}^{3}-y-0.5{x}_{\text{new}}-0.5x=0.
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.5$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}+{y}_{\text{new}}+0.25{y}^{3}-y-0.5{x}_{\text{new}}-0.5x.
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is

$$
{x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=0.5+0.5=1.
$$

Then, the function $g$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & =0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}+{y}_{\text{new}}+0.25(1)^{3}-1-0.5\cdot 1-0.5\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.25({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}+{y}_{\text{new}}-1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

We use a root-finding method with starting point $y=1$ to solve $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.$ We'll use Newton's method:

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{g({y}_{\text{new}})}{{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})}
$$

Note that the derivative of $g$ is

$$
{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})=0.75({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton's method iterative scheme is as follows:

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{0.25(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})^{3}+({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-1.5}{0.75(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})^{2}+1}
$$

Applying several iterations of Newton's method starting with $y(0.5)=1,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}_{\text{new}})_{1} & =1 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{2} & ≈1.142\,857 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{3} & ≈1.134\,757 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{4} & ≈1.134\,728\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(1)≈1.13,$ rounded to two decimal places.
